title: Dilated eye exam
what: The doctor puts in drops to widen your pupils. This gives a better view of the retina at the back of the eye.
why: For diabetes, high blood pressure, nearsightedness, flashes or floaters, and routine checkups.
duration: usually 30 to 60 minutes including waiting for the drops; vision stays blurry for another 4 to 6 hours
tell_doctor: Glaucoma or high eye pressure, if you know

prepare.title: Getting there
prepare.text: After the drops, you cannot drive for a few hours. Come with someone or take a taxi.

prepare.title: Your day
prepare.text: For a few hours it will be hard to read or look at screens. Plan your day.

bring: Someone to drive you, if you usually drive
steps: The doctor checks your vision and eye pressure
You wait 20 to 40 minutes for the pupils to widen
The doctor shines a light in your eye and looks through a lens
You are asked to look in different directions
feel: The bright light is unpleasant, but brief
For a few hours, close-up vision is blurry and light feels glaring
after: Do not drive until your vision is back to normal
If you wear contacts, put them back in when your doctor says
red_flags: Severe eye pain, headache, nausea, and rainbow rings around lights after the drops: see an eye doctor urgently or call emergency services

faq.q: How long do the pupils stay wide?
faq.a: Usually 4 to 6 hours, sometimes up to a day.
Usually yes, but reading and screens will be hard for a few hours.

reminders.text: Dilated eye exam tomorrow. Do not plan to drive. Bring sunglasses.
